name: LemurSaucePacket
description: A Create-powered SMP that still feels like Minecraft. Build factories, rail networks and airships, explore a reworked world, and fight your way up the ages.

shaderPresets._comment: The launcher shader picker (Settings > Graphics). Iris is always installed with shaders off by default; each preset names a shader pack by its packwiz file (pack/shaderpacks/<shaderpack>.pw.toml), which publish.mjs turns into the zip name. (Key renamed from "shaders" in launcher 0.1.6, so 0.1.5 hides its picker instead of misreading this.)

presets.name: Lite
presets.description: MakeUp Ultra Fast. Soft lighting, shadows and water for any PC that can run the pack.

presets.name: Balanced
presets.description: Complementary Reimagined. Keeps the Minecraft look with good shadows, water and sky. Needs a decent graphics card.

presets.name: Fancy
presets.description: Complementary Unbound. The most realistic lighting, clouds and reflections. For strong graphics cards.

news.title: 1.14.2: Photos for the wiki's atlas
news.body: The wiki's atlas has photos now, taken in game: 207 of the pack's 227 biomes and all 119 creatures. Biomes nobody could find in the photo world, or that didn't photograph well, keep their painted cards for now. Distant Horizons is back on its own default way of building far land: 1.14.1's change didn't help and only made it slower to fill in.

news.title: 1.14: A skills screen, the wiki in game, distant land and Climbing Boots
news.body: ESC → Skills (or /skills) opens a skills screen of its own, like RuneScape's skills tab: every skill with its level and progress, your total level, combat level and total XP. Hover a skill for what trains it, what each level gives and what it unlocks next; click it, or a skill in the inventory's panel, for its guide: every level that unlocks something, down a track lit to your level, with the XP to the next unlock. The Guide button opens this wiki in a browser inside the game (it fetches its engine once, the first time the game starts). Distant Horizons draws the land beyond your render distance, 2,048 blocks out (Video Settings → Distant Horizons). Auto walk is on the ` key (walk backwards to stop). The HUD Layout editor resizes as well as moves: drag a box's corner, roll the wheel over it or press + and -. A new relic, the Climbing Boots, steps you up full blocks without jumping: Crafting 20 to make, Agility 25 to wear. A new world's capital now suits the land it's built in (sand in a desert, snow on snowy plains) and eases into the hills around it. ReForgedPlay (Replay Mod) is installed for making videos; it records nothing until you turn it on.

news.title: 1.13: Hiscores, and Create's machines join the skills
news.body: The hiscores: /hiscores ranks everyone on the server RuneScape-style, by every skill, total and combat level, quest points, capes, the collection log, monsters slain, bosses (Elvarg, Kiln-Tok-Jad, Kiln-Kal-Zuk, the Ender Dragon, the Wither, the Warden and more) and collections (music discs, armour trims, pottery sherds, relics, mob heads). /hiscores player <name> shows anyone's. Create's machines now wait on the skill they take over: Mining 15 for mechanical drills, Woodcutting 15 for saws, Farming 15 for harvesters and ploughs, Cooking 20 for encased fans, Crafting 30 for mechanical crafters, Construction 30 for the schematicannon, Smithing 35 for steam engines, Agility 35 for train stations and controls, Enchanting 35 for the blaze enchanter and 50 for the printer, and Mining 50 and up for the ore vein drill heads. Anyone can use a machine someone else made. Construction's saving perk now only ever saves building blocks: never storage blocks, copper, coin stacks or anything that holds items.

news.title: 1.12: Construction and the Mason’s Palette
news.body: Construction is the sixteenth skill: every block you place pays XP once it has stood for a minute, and the fancier the block the more (cobblestone pays 2, Macaw's roofs and furniture 15, a lectern or a sea lantern 25); placing and breaking pays nothing. Each level adds a 0.1% chance a block isn't used up, and Construction unlocks twelve crafting recipes for decorative blocks in bulk (ten stone bricks from eight stone and a clay ball, cracked and mossy kinds without a furnace, eight stairs where vanilla gives four). At 99 the Construction Cape comes with the Mason's Palette: choose a block (stone of every kind, bricks, quartz, concrete, glass, Create's cut stone, Create Deco, Macaw's stone and metal blocks, lanterns, lecterns) and place as many as you like. What it places drops nothing when broken, so it can't be farmed. Lost it? Gerta the Mason makes another. The Maxed Cape now asks for Construction 99 too. The Builder's Wand and the Harvester's Scythe now respect safe zones like Lemurton.

news.title: 1.11: Skills that unlock things
news.body: Every skill now unlocks things on the way to 99, like a RuneScape skill guide: Crafting 30 makes diamond gear, Smithing 50 netherite, the bigger meals wait on Cooking, and Farming and Woodcutting gate the rarer crops and trees. Brewing is the fifteenth skill: each potion you take out of a stand trains it, each ingredient waits on a level, and Brewing 55 makes Eyes of Ender, so it's also the way to the Ender Dragon. Wither skeletons drop skulls only at combat level 75, treasure on the line needs Fishing 20, and crossbows and tridents moved to Ranged. Enchantments past their vanilla level also need the gear's own skill to use: Fishing for Lure, Mining for Fortune, Attack for Sharpness. Your combat level shows under your name. The bigger main quests ask for levels first (Dragon Slayer I: combat 40 and Brewing 55). Each gear set takes a hand-made part, and machines (the Crafter, Create's crafters, mixer and press) won't make anything gated. The Brewing Cape makes potions last half as long again.

news.title: 1.10: Capes you can hold
news.body: Capes are items now. When you earn one it lands in your bag: right-click it, or put it in the new Cape slot in the Curios panel (only someone who earned it can wear it). Any cape can hang on an armor stand: right-click the stand with it, sneak and right-click with an empty hand to take it back. ESC → Capes is your collection: every cape, how far along you are, each perk, and who makes another if you lose one (Odo the Tailor in Lemurton, 99,000 coins for a skill cape; Brakka at Kiln Hollow for the pit capes, or win again: every win hands one over). Also: the Infernal Cape is redrawn so it burns from the hem up, the Gold Coins look like vanilla's gold, and Lemurton's townsfolk pick up new dialogs by themselves.

news.title: 1.9: Dragon Slayer I and II
news.body: Dragon Slayer I is now the Ender Dragon. Oziach puts the three map pieces together into a Map to the Stronghold; light its portal, break her crystals, and everyone with the map who is near her when she falls gets her head. Then Dragon Slayer II: Wizard Traiborn scries the isle of Crandor with two bottles of her breath, and Ned takes you up to Elvarg's Lair as before. Dragon armour now waits on Dragon Slayer II; the Fight Pits open after Dragon Slayer I, and Ashes of the Kiln asks for Dragon Slayer II in place of the Ender Dragon. Lost the Anti-dragon Shield? The mayor has Brann copy it for 2,000 coins.

news.title: 1.8: The Fight Pits and the Inferno
news.body: After Dragon Slayer I, Guildmaster Greaves sends you to the Kilnfolk, ashen piglins in the volcanic lands. At Kiln Hollow, earn the right to fight in the Fight Pits: thirty waves alone, then Kiln-Tok-Jad, whose fire you block with a shield and whose slam you run from. Win the animated Fire Cape. Then Ashes of the Kiln (the Wither, the Ender Dragon, the Warden and an Infernal Key) opens the Inferno, where Kiln-Kal-Zuk burns everyone his drifting shield does not cover: survive it for the Infernal Cape. Fall in either and you are pulled out with everything you had. Also: the legendary capes are redrawn as proper pixel art, and the custom armour sets look like themselves when worn.

news.title: A new world, and Elvarg's Lair
news.body: The server starts over on a fresh world. Follow the compass you get to Lemurton, a short walk from spawn. Dragon Slayer I now ends in Elvarg's Lair: speak to Ned at the Crandor memorial and fight her alone or with up to three friends; if she gets you, Ned keeps your things. The pack also has a website now, play.limas.ca, with the wiki, a gallery and every update.

news.title: 1.1: Gear, capes and the guide
news.body: The Armory is open: a tree-felling Lumber Axe, an Excavator's 3x3 pickaxe, a Prospector's pickaxe that smelts what it mines, a Harvester's Scythe, a Builder's Wand, three weapons and five armour sets with full-set bonuses (Prospector, Aeronaut, Brass Duelist, Compacted Diamond, Compacted Netherite). All Create-made and skill-gated; the rarest pieces only drop in dungeons. Relics is in, with set synergies. Capes: earn them from skills at 99, finished chapters and real feats; ESC → Capes. And every page of the new wiki is in your inventory as the LemurSaucePacket Guide (ESC → Guide).

news.title: Welcome to LemurSaucePacket
news.body: Press Play. The launcher installs Minecraft, NeoForge and every mod for you, keeps them in sync with the server, and drops you straight in.
